subject: scallop
title: This Animal Has 200 Eyes, and Every One Is a Mirror

scenes.text: This animal has two hundred eyes. And none of them uses a lens.
It's the scallop. Its eyes line the edge of the shell, each about a millimeter across.
Instead of a lens, each eye has a tiny curved mirror at the back.
The mirror is built from stacked layers of flat, perfectly square crystals of guanine.
Light bounces off and focuses onto two different retinas. One sees movement. One sees dim edges.
That's a telescope, in a shellfish. Two hundred of them, watching for the first shadow.

description:
This animal has two hundred eyes, and none of them uses a lens.
Scallop eyes use mirrors made of flat square guanine crystals to focus light onto two retinas.
What is the strangest eye you know of?
first_comment: Scallops see with mirrors, not lenses. Which animal should we show next with a weird sense?
